functions.name: oatpp::Logger::log
functions.signature: virtual void oatpp::Logger::log(v_uint32 priority, const std::string& tag, const std::string& message) = 0
functions.description: Pure virtual logging entry point for all log messages. Implementations should emit or process a message with the given priority, tag, and text. Used by OATPP_LOG* macros and Environment::log.
requirements: Must be implemented by a concrete Logger before use.
Callers may pass any string for tag and message; no stated size limits beyond any enforced by an implementation.
Priority is an integer level; typical values are one of Logger::PRIORITY_V/D/I/W/E.

functions.name: oatpp::Logger::isLogPriorityEnabled
functions.description: Query whether a given priority should be logged/printed by this logger. Default implementation returns true; concrete loggers may filter.
requirements: Input is a priority level; typical values are Logger::PRIORITY_V/D/I/W/E.
No side effects are specified.

functions.name: oatpp::Logger::getMaxFormattingBufferSize
functions.description: Returns the maximum number of bytes that should be allocated for formatting a single log message. Default returns 4096.
requirements: No input requirements.
Callers should not allocate a larger buffer for formatting a message than the returned value if they follow the logger’s recommendation.

functions.name: oatpp::LogCategory::enablePriority
functions.description: Enable logging of a specific priority level for this category by setting the corresponding bit in the category’s enabledPriorities mask.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values; the implementation uses it as a bit index (1 << priority).
Category must be constructed before calling.

functions.name: oatpp::LogCategory::disablePriority
functions.description: Disable logging of a specific priority level for this category by clearing the corresponding bit in the enabledPriorities mask.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values; the implementation uses it as a bit index (1 << priority).
Category must be constructed before calling.

functions.name: oatpp::LogCategory::isLogPriorityEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether the given priority should be logged/printed for this category, considering both categoryEnabled and enabledPriorities.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values.

functions.name: oatpp::DefaultLogger::DefaultLogger
functions.signature: oatpp::DefaultLogger::DefaultLogger(const Config& config = Config("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", true, (1 << PRIORITY_V) | (1 << PRIORITY_D) | (1 << PRIORITY_I) | (1 << PRIORITY_W) | (1 << PRIORITY_E)))
functions.description: Constructs the default logger with the provided configuration (time format, whether to print microsecond ticks, and an initial log-mask). When used without arguments, initializes with a timestamp, ticks, and all priorities enabled.
requirements: Config::timeFormat may be nullptr to disable time printing (per comment on timeFormat).
Config::logMask is a bitmap; bits correspond to (1 << PRIORITY_*).
No lifetime requirement for the passed Config since it is copied into the logger.

functions.name: oatpp::DefaultLogger::log
functions.signature: void oatpp::DefaultLogger::log(v_uint32 priority, const std::string& tag, const std::string& message) override
functions.description: Thread-safe log emission that formats and prints the message according to the logger configuration, if the priority is enabled by the log mask.
requirements: priority should be a valid priority (Logger::PRIORITY_*).
Tag and message may be any strings; size may be bounded by getMaxFormattingBufferSize() in implementations.

functions.name: oatpp::DefaultLogger::enablePriority
functions.description: Enable logging of a priority level in this logger instance by setting the corresponding bit in the internal log mask.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values (used as bit index).

functions.name: oatpp::DefaultLogger::disablePriority
functions.description: Disable logging of a priority level in this logger instance by clearing the corresponding bit in the internal log mask.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values (used as bit index).

functions.name: oatpp::DefaultLogger::isLogPriorityEnabled
functions.description: Returns whether the given priority is currently enabled for this logger instance, according to its log mask.
requirements: priority should correspond to one of Logger::PRIORITY_* values.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::init
functions.description: Initializes the oatpp environment and performs basic health-checks. Sets up global state (e.g., logger) prior to use of other environment-managed features.
requirements: Should be called before using other Environment features that depend on initialization.
Thread-safety/allowed repetition is not specified; typical usage is to call once per process.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::destroy
functions.description: De-initializes the oatpp environment and performs health checks, including checking for memory leaks (object counter mismatches).
requirements: Should be called during shutdown after Environment::init.
Callers should not use environment-managed components after this call.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::incObjects
functions.description: Increments the global object counter. Used internally to track allocations of oatpp objects.
requirements: Intended for internal use by oatpp object lifecycle hooks; external callers should ensure increments are balanced with decObjects().

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::decObjects
functions.description: Decrements the global object counter. Used internally to track deallocations of oatpp objects.
requirements: Should be balanced with prior calls to incObjects() to maintain correct counts.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getObjectsCount
functions.description: Returns the number of oatpp-tracked objects currently allocated and stored in memory.
requirements: None.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getObjectsCreated
functions.description: Returns the total number of oatpp-tracked objects created during the process lifetime.
requirements: None.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getThreadLocalObjectsCount
functions.description: Returns the number of oatpp-tracked objects currently allocated in the calling thread. Returns 0 if built with -DOATPP_COMPAT_BUILD_NO_THREAD_LOCAL.
requirements: Only meaningful if the build supports thread_local; otherwise always 0.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getThreadLocalObjectsCreated
functions.description: Returns the total number of oatpp-tracked objects created in the calling thread. Returns 0 if built with -DOATPP_COMPAT_BUILD_NO_THREAD_LOCAL.
requirements: Only meaningful if the build supports thread_local; otherwise always 0.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::setLogger
functions.description: Sets the system-wide environment logger to the provided instance.
requirements: logger should be a valid shared_ptr to a Logger implementation; behavior for nullptr is not documented.
Can be called after init to change the logger.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getLogger
functions.description: Returns the current system-wide environment logger.
requirements: May return nullptr if no logger is set (not documented but possible depending on initialization).

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::printCompilationConfig
functions.description: Prints debug information about the compilation configuration, including values such as OATPP_DISABLE_ENV_OBJECT_COUNTERS and OATPP_THREAD_HARDWARE_CONCURRENCY.
requirements: None; produces output via the logger or stdout as implemented.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::log
functions.signature: static void oatpp::Environment::log(v_uint32 priority, const std::string& tag, const std::string& message)
functions.description: Convenience method that forwards the given message to the current environment Logger::log().
requirements: Environment should be initialized and a logger set for output to occur.
priority should be a valid Logger priority (PRIORITY_V/D/I/W/E).

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getComponent
functions.description: Returns a component object registered under the given type name (typeid(T).name()). If multiple components of the same type exist, the behavior depends on registration; this overload does not disambiguate by name.
requirements: typeName must match the registration name used by Environment::Component<T>, i.e., typeid(T).name().
Returned pointer is a raw void*; caller must cast to the correct type and ensure the component’s lifetime remains valid.

functions.name: oatpp::Environment::getMicroTickCount
functions.description: Returns the current tick count in microseconds for timing/logging purposes.
requirements: None stated; returns a timestamp-like monotonic value as implemented.

functions.name: oatpp::isValidIOHandle
functions.description: Returns true if the provided I/O handle is valid (i.e., not equal to INVALID_IO_HANDLE for the platform).
requirements: handle should be an OS-provided I/O handle (e.g., file descriptor or socket handle).

functions.name: oatpp::AsyncIOError::AsyncIOError
functions.description: Constructs an asynchronous I/O error with a descriptive type string and an I/O error code (from IOError).
requirements: code should be one of the defined IOError values (e.g., BROKEN_PIPE, RETRY_READ, RETRY_WRITE, ZERO_VALUE).
what must be a valid C-string describing the error type.

functions.name: oatpp::AsyncIOError::getCode
functions.description: Returns the stored asynchronous I/O error code associated with this error object.
requirements: None.

data_types.description: A generic byte string with no required encoding or structure. May contain any bytes including ASCII, UTF-8, or binary data. Used wherever std::string inputs are accepted without format constraints.

A NUL-terminated C-style string pointer that may also be null. When non-null, contents are arbitrary and not required to follow any particular format; when null, the callee interprets it as disabling or defaulting behavior.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets std::string inputs used by logger/category/environment fuzzers.
# We aim to produce valid, interesting strings within 4096 bytes, covering:
# - Typical log tags/messages (ASCII words, timestamps, JSON, long lines)
# - Edge cases (empty, very long near buffer limit 4096, UTF-8, binary, null bytes)
# - Time-format-like strings for DefaultLogger::Config (strftime patterns, nullptr handled by fuzzer)
# The fuzzer will reuse the provided buffer across multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FILENAME calls,
# so we pack multiple strings separated by a delimiter to provide rich content.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096
DELIM = b"\n---\n"  # delimiter between entries


def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-:.#/[](){}<>@$%^&*+?=,|" \
        + "\t\r\n"
    s = ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n))
    return s.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # mix of scripts and emoji
    pools = [
        (0x0020, 0x007E),   # ASCII printable
        (0x00A0, 0x024F),   # Latin-1/Extended
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),   # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),   # Cyrillic
        (0x3040, 0x30FF),   # Hiragana/Katakana
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),   # CJK Unified
        (0x1F300, 0x1F64F), # Emojis
    ]
    out: List[int] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        lo, hi = r.choice(pools)
        out.append(r.randint(lo, hi))
    return ''.join(chr(c) for c in out).encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _rand_binary(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return bytes(r.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _timestamp_like(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Common timestamp formats used by DefaultLogger timeFormat
    fmts = [
        "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
        "%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S",
        "%d-%b-%Y %H:%M:%S",
        "%H:%M:%S",
        "%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z",
        "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f",
        "%s"  # epoch seconds
    ]
    # Also include some variants
    fmts += ["%Q-%W-%E %R:%T:%Z", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z", "[%Y/%m/%d] %H:%M:%S"]
    return r.choice(fmts).encode()


def _json_like(r: random.Random, max_kv: int = 6) -> bytes:
    kv = r.randint(0, max_kv)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(kv):
        key = _rand_ascii(r, 1, 10).decode('utf-8', 'ignore').replace('"', '')
        choice = r.randint(0, 4)
        if choice == 0:
            val = '"' + _rand_ascii(r, 0, 20).decode('utf-8', 'ignore').replace('"', '') + '"'
        elif choice == 1:
            val = str(r.randint(-1_000_000, 1_000_000))
        elif choice == 2:
            val = 'true' if r.random() < 0.5 else 'false'
        elif choice == 3:
            val = 'null'
        else:
            val = '"' + _rand_utf8(r, 1, 8).decode('utf-8', 'ignore').replace('"', '') + '"'
        parts.append(f'"{key}": {val}')
    return ('{' + ', '.join(parts) + '}').encode('utf-8', 'ignore')


def _long_repeated(r: random.Random, token: bytes, min_rep: int, max_rep: int) -> bytes:
    reps = r.randint(min_rep, max_rep)
    return token * reps


def _priority_tag(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    tags = [b"VERBOSE", b"DEBUG", b"INFO", b"WARN", b"ERROR",
            b"net", b"io", b"db", b"auth", b"startup", b"shutdown"]
    return r.choice(tags)


def _compose_entries(r: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[bytes]:
    entries: List[bytes] = []
    # Include a mix to satisfy various FUZZ_PARAM_STR use-sites
    candidates = [
        _priority_tag(r),
        b"oatpp", b"logger", b"category", b"env", b"component",
        _timestamp_like(r),
        _json_like(r),
        _rand_ascii(r, 0, 64),
        _rand_ascii(r, 128, 512),
        _rand_utf8(r, 4, 64),
        _rand_utf8(r, 64, 256),
        _long_repeated(r, b"A", 50, 500),
        _long_repeated(r, b" ", 10, 200),
        b"tag:service/api/v1", b"message:operation completed",
        b"multi\nline\nmessage",
        b"contains\0null",  # include a null byte marker
        _rand_binary(r, 8, 64),
        _rand_binary(r, 256, 512),
    ]
    # Shuffle and add until budget
    r.shuffle(candidates)
    total = 0
    for c in candidates:
        if total + len(c) + len(DELIM) > budget:
            remain = max(0, budget - total - len(DELIM))
            if remain > 0:
                entries.append(c[:remain])
                total += remain + len(DELIM)
            break
        entries.append(c)
        total += len(c) + len(DELIM)
    return entries


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide overall size under MAX_TOTAL
    target = r.randint(256, MAX_TOTAL)

    # Ensure we include at least one time-format candidate and one long message near buffer limit
    entries = _compose_entries(r, target - 64)

    # Add dedicated timeFormat-like entry
    entries.append(_timestamp_like(r))

    # Add a long near-limit message to exercise truncation to getMaxFormattingBufferSize()
    near_limit_len = min(4096, max(512, target // 2))
    # Build long payload with controlled repetition bounds
    core_len = max(0, near_limit_len - 8)
    long_core = _long_repeated(r, b"x", max(1, core_len // 2), max(1, core_len))
    long_msg = (_priority_tag(r) + b":" + long_core)[:near_limit_len]
    entries.append(long_msg)

    # Shuffle entries for variability
    r.shuffle(entries)

    # Join with delimiter and ensure total size constraint
    buf = DELIM.join(entries)
    if len(buf) > MAX_TOTAL:
        buf = buf[:MAX_TOTAL]

    return bytes(buf)

import random
import struct
import itertools

# This generator targets inputs consumed by FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM for
# oatpp::DefaultLogger::Config where timeFormat is a nullable C-string.
# The fuzzer stub uses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() for a std::string whose c_str() may be
# passed as const char* (or nullptr chosen via another FUZZ_PARAM). Our buffer
# should therefore provide an interesting ASCII/UTF-8 string payload followed by
# additional bytes for numeric parameters consumed by FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and
# FUZZ_PARAM(v_uint32). We pack multiple fields to let the harness slice out data.
#
# Layout we emit (little-endian for integers):
# [section_count u8]
# Repeated sections, each: [type u8][len u16][payload bytes]
# Types:
#  1: time format C-string content (payload excludes final NUL; we ensure it is NUL-terminated by appending 0 on extraction length)
#  2: unsigned int (4 bytes)
#  3: v_uint32 (4 bytes)
#  4: boolean hint byte for printMicroTicks (0/1)
#  5: prebuilt common time format literal (no payload; decoder maps to literal)
#
# The fuzzer framework will not decode this format, but packing multiple values
# sequentially ensures FUZZ_PARAM_STR and subsequent FUZZ_PARAM reads consume
# deterministic bytes in order. The std::string read will grab a slice until the
# next NUL byte; we therefore place a NUL after our chosen time-format string and
# keep following numeric bytes after that.

COMMON_TIME_FORMATS = [
    b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
    b"%H:%M:%S",
    b"%Y-%m-%d",
    b"%c",
    b"%F %T",
    b"%Y-%j %H:%M:%S",
    b"%s",  # epoch seconds in some libs
    b"",     # empty string to test "no format" but non-null
]

VERBOSE_TAGS = [
    b"NET",
    b"DB",
    b"AUTH",
    b"CACHE",
    b"WORKER",
]


def _rand_timefmt(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        return rng.choice(COMMON_TIME_FORMATS)
    elif choice == 1:
        # Include microseconds pattern
        return b"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.%f"
    elif choice == 2:
        # Include timezone offset placeholder often seen
        return b"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"
    elif choice == 3:
        # ISO8601-like with Z
        return b"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"
    elif choice == 4:
        # Custom with brackets and literal text
        return b"[%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S] LOG"
    else:
        # Random printable pattern including percent tokens and letters
        tokens = [b"%Y", b"%m", b"%d", b"%H", b"%M", b"%S", b"%f", b"%z", b"%j"]
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            if rng.random() < 0.7:
                parts.append(rng.choice(tokens))
            else:
                # separator chunk
                sep_len = rng.randint(0, 3)
                seps = b"-/:T .[]_"
                parts.append(bytes(rng.choice(seps) for _ in range(sep_len)))
        s = b"".join(parts)
        if rng.random() < 0.4 and s:
            s = s + b" " + rng.choice(VERBOSE_TAGS)
        return s


def _pack_u32(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate values interesting for mask computations: full mask, single bits, alternating, zeros, random
    choices = [
        0x00000000,
        0xFFFFFFFF,
        0xAAAAAAAA,
        0x55555555,
        1 << rng.randrange(0, 32),
        (1 << 5) - 1,  # 5-bit all ones
        rng.getrandbits(32),
    ]
    val = rng.choice(choices)
    return struct.pack('<I', val & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _pack_uint(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # unsigned int assumed 32-bit in most builds; provide same as u32
    return _pack_u32(rng)


def _bool_byte(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    return b"\x01" if rng.random() < 0.5 else b"\x00"


def _build_buffer(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Build a layout that starts with a NUL-terminated time format for FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
    # After that, we place bytes for FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) and FUZZ_PARAM(v_uint32),
    # which the harness will draw to decide nullptr usage, printTicks, and mask.

    buf = bytearray()

    # Primary string: either empty, common, or random with valid UTF-8-ish bytes.
    tfmt = _rand_timefmt(rng)
    # Ensure length reasonable
    if len(tfmt) > 200:
        tfmt = tfmt[:200]
    buf += tfmt
    buf += b"\x00"  # NUL terminator so std::string(c_str) read sees proper termination in source fuzz data

    # Provide a couple of unsigned ints for modulo decisions used by stubs
    # The stub does two FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int) calls before computing printTicks/nullptr.
    # We'll emit multiple 4-byte ints to satisfy potential multiple reads.
    for _ in range(3):
        buf += _pack_uint(rng)

    # Provide a v_uint32 for mask source
    for _ in range(2):
        buf += _pack_u32(rng)

    # Also provide an explicit boolean hint for printTicks in case consumed as byte elsewhere
    buf += _bool_byte(rng)

    # Pad with additional plausible time format strings separated by NUL to give variety
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        extra_count = rng.randint(1, 3)
        for _ in range(extra_count):
            s = _rand_timefmt(rng)
            if len(s) > 128:
                s = s[:128]
            buf += s + b"\x00"

    # Truncate to max size constraint
    return bytes(buf[:4096])


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_buffer(rng)
